extra.message: payroll_bundle_thaw_186 passes attacker-controlled data (request body or 'blob' GET parameter, optionally base64-decoded) directly to pickle.loads(). Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary remote code execution.

extra.message: payroll_formula_cast_268 evaluates the user-supplied 'expr' GET parameter with eval(). Even with __builtins__ removed, eval on attacker input is exploitable (object graph traversal to reach os/subprocess), leading to remote code execution.

extra.message: payroll_jinja_cast_685 concatenates the user-controlled 'fragment' GET parameter into a Jinja2 Template and renders it. This is server-side template injection (SSTI), allowing the attacker to access the object graph and achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: payroll_mongo_lane_714 takes the attacker-controlled JSON body ('filter' key or entire payload) and passes it directly as the query document to MongoDB find_one(). This allows NoSQL injection via operator objects (e.g. {"$gt": ""}, "$where") to bypass filters and extract records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: payroll_vault_stash_246 builds a file path from the user-controlled 'ref' GET parameter (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without sanitization and writes to it. cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: payroll_dock_shelf_722 uses the user-controlled 'name' GET parameter as the output file name (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and writes the raw request body to it. cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: payroll_badge_gate_694 grants the 'elevated' lane with full payroll and casework access based solely on a client-controlled cookie (ops_badge) or header (x-ops-badge) being equal to 'lead'. extra.message: payroll_wayback_card_105 redirects to the unvalidated 'lane' GET parameter via redirect(next_url). An attacker can supply an external URL, enabling open redirect phishing attacks.
